reason: No principle reconciles the affirmation of an enduring subject with its denial without erasing a distinction both sides insist on (NBh 1.1.2; Tattvasaṅgraha Ātmaparīkṣā).

change: partially reconciled: conventional causation vs ultimate non-origination (Advaita, Madhyamaka) under P1-level
reason: Śaṅkara and Nāgārjuna themselves assign causal transformation / dependent arising to the conventional and deny real origination ultimately.

change: partially reconciled: pre-existence and novelty of the effect under P2-standpoint (the Jains' own anekānta)
reason: Tattvārthasūtra 5.30 and Sanmati 3.53 state the synthesis in the Jains' own terms; Sāṃkhya and Nyāya reject it.

change: remainder queued RQ-U50-02 (Sāṃkhya vs Nyāya; vivarta vs ābhāsa; apparent vs real transformation of Brahman)
reason: The parties insist on the distinction; no principle reconciles it without erasing it.

change: queued RQ-U50-03; candidate readings P1, P2, P4 and the vivarta/ābhāsa distinction recorded with objections
reason: Advaita's levels of reality are rejected as such by the theistic Vedāntas and reinterpreted by Kashmir Śaivism; no reconciliation without erasing a distinction the traditions insist on.

change: queued RQ-U50-04; candidate readings P1, P2, P3, P4 recorded with the objections of Dvaita, Advaita and Viśiṣṭādvaita
reason: Each school insists its reading of the same texts is their purport; Madhva explicitly denies any identity.

change: queued RQ-U50-05; doctrinal charge kept apart from the historical borrowing evidence (brw:madhyamaka-to-gaudapada, brw:yogacara-to-gaudapada)
reason: Advaita and its critics disagree whether the difference between sat-cit Brahman and śūnyatā is decisive or verbal; no principle settles this without erasing a distinction both insist on.

change: partially reconciled under P4-stage: sudden and gradual assigned to faculties of practitioners (the traditions' own principle)
reason: Platform Sūtra 7.3, Zongmi, Jinul, the Ājñāsamyakpramāṇa and the Varāha Upaniṣad state it in their own terms.

change: partially reconciled under P1-level: principle (li) awakened suddenly, phenomena (shi) removed gradually
reason: Śūraṅgama 10 and Zongmi's sun-and-frost simile distinguish the two aspects.

change: remainder queued RQ-U50-06: Samye (non-examining vs correct analysis); Seongcheol vs Jinul; Kathāvatthu vs Sarvāstivāda
reason: Kamalaśīla denies any way other than analysis; Seongcheol denies gradual cultivation after true awakening.

change: partially reconciled under P4-stage (study/reflection vs meditation) and P3-path, in the Rimé and Nyingma traditions' own terms
reason: Kongtrul and Mipham themselves state the reconciliation; Gelug, Jonang and Gorampa reject it.

change: remainder queued RQ-U50-07: whether the ultimate is truly established (Jonang) or empty of own-nature (Gelug)
reason: Both parties explicitly deny the other's ultimate; P5-neyartha applied in opposite directions.

change: partially reconciled under P4-stage (enumerated vs non-enumerated ultimate) and P6-upaya (method of leading the opponent), per Mipham and the Sakya reading
reason: Mipham states the sequence in his own terms; the Indian parties share the conclusion of MMK 1.1.

change: remainder queued RQ-U50-08: Gelug holds a difference of view (own-character conventionally)
reason: Tsongkhapa rejects any reading that makes the difference merely methodological.

change: partially reconciled under P4-stage: works as purification preceding knowledge; grace graded by the means that wins it
reason: BSBh 3.4.26, the Bhāmatī and Madhva's gradation state this order in the traditions' own terms.

change: partially reconciled under P3-path: knowledge, action and devotion as yogas for different people
reason: BhG 3.3 and Uddhava Gītā 11.20.6-8 assign the paths to temperaments.

change: remainder queued RQ-U50-09 (samuccaya vs knowledge alone; devotion as means or goal; prapatti as means or not; self-power vs other-power)
reason: Śaṅkara and Bhāskara, the Vaṭakalai and Teṅkalai, and the Pure Land schools each deny the other's thesis.

change: queued RQ-U50-10; candidate readings P1, P2 (Haribhadra), P3 (Yoga) recorded with objections
reason: Affirmation and denial of a world-maker cannot be reconciled without erasing a distinction each side insists on.

change: queued RQ-U50-11; Vedānta's middle course and the Upaniṣadic relativization recorded as candidate readings (P2, P1/P4, P7)
reason: Authorless vs Lord-authored vs rejected: each side explicitly denies the others' basis of authority.

change: queued RQ-U50-12; the orthodox eligibility/liberation distinction recorded as partial narrowing, not reconciliation
reason: The Digambara–Śvetāmbara disagreement and the critique of birth-based adhikāra are explicitly maintained by the parties.

change: partially reconciled under P3-path (Gītā 12: both worshippers reach him)
reason: The Gītā itself states it.

change: partially reconciled under P1-level (Advaita: qualified Brahman for worship, unqualified for knowledge)
reason: BSBh 1.1.12 states the twofold Brahman in Advaita's own terms.

change: partially reconciled under P2-standpoint (BhP 1.2.11 three names; Tulsīdās; Trika's transcendent-and-immanent)
reason: The Bhāgavata, the Rāmcaritmānas and Kṣemarāja state both as true of the one reality.

change: remainder queued RQ-U50-13: which is higher, and whether the qualities are real
reason: Advaita and the Gauḍīyas rank in opposite directions; Rāmānuja and Madhva deny nirguṇa Brahman.

change: partially reconciled under P4-stage: means graded by intensity of grace (Trika) and effort joined with guru's grace (haṭha)
reason: Tantrāloka 1.168-170 / 13.300-301 and HYP 3.2-5 state the pairing in their own terms.

change: partially reconciled under P3-path: practice-and-dispassion or devotion to Īśvara as alternative means
reason: YS 1.12-23 offers effort and devotion as alternatives.

change: remainder queued RQ-U50-14: effortful arousal vs innate/effortless state as liberation; grace free vs grace upon ripened mala
reason: The Amaraughaśāsana and Amanaska deny what the haṭha texts affirm.

change: partially reconciled under P2-standpoint: counts differ by classification; the schools' own inclusion (antarbhāva) arguments
reason: NS 2.2.1-2, the Tattvakaumudī, Praśastapāda, Madhva and the Yatīndramatadīpikā each include the others' extra means.

change: remainder queued RQ-U50-15: denial of inference (Cārvāka); testimony for the supersensible; no fixed means (Madhyamaka, Jayarāśi)
reason: The parties insist these are substantive, not classificatory.

change: stages banded: 1 yama=B1; 2 niyama=B1; 3 āsana=B2; 4 prāṇāyāma=B2; 5 pratyāhāra=B3; 6 dhāraṇā=B3; 7 dhyāna=B3; 8 samādhi=B4
reason: Banded by what each limb is in the sūtra: restraints and observances are the ethical-purificatory foundation (B1); posture and breath preparatory discipline (B2); withdrawal, concentration and meditation one-pointedness (B3); samādhi as a limb is object-supported absorption (B4). Nothing in the eight limbs is itself B5+; YS 2.28 names viveka-khyāti as their fruit.
Same eight limb-names re-described in the Yoga Yājñavalkya (ten yamas and ten niyamas; prāṇāyāma with nāḍī-purification).
Tirumūlar's eightfold (aṭṭāṅka) yoga in Tamil uses the same eight limbs inside a Śaiva frame.
The Purāṇic eight limbs follow the Pātañjala order.
Haribhadra himself pairs his eight views with the eight limbs (YDS 16), reinterpreting the limbs inwardly.
Five limb-names shared (without yama, niyama, āsana; with tarka); older six-limbed scheme.
The Gheraṇḍa replaces yama/niyama with the six cleansing acts and adds mudrā; four limb-names shared.

change: stages banded: 1 savitarkā samāpatti=B4; 2 nirvitarkā samāpatti=B4; 3 savicārā samāpatti=B4; 4 nirvicārā samāpatti=B4; 5 sānanda=B4; 6 sāsmitā=B4; 7 adhyātma-prasāda, ṛtambharā prajñā, vive=B5; 8 asamprajñāta / nirbīja samādhi=B6; 9 dharmamegha samādhi=B6; 10 kaivalya=B7
reason: The samprajñāta coalescences and forms (vitarka→asmitā) are absorption with support (B4); truth-bearing insight and viveka-khyāti are the first direct seeing of the difference of puruṣa and sattva (B5); asamprajñāta/nirbīja and dharmamegha deepen that stilling (B6); kaivalya is final liberation (B7). Consistent with U10's pth:rajamartanda-samadhi-ladder and pth:yoga-sutra-kaivalya-sequence.
Bhoja's version of the same ladder (RM 1.17-18) with viveka-khyāti as a seventh samprajñāta rung.
Continuation of the top of this ladder in YS 4.25-34 (same dharmamegha → kaivalya segment).
Both are graded absorptions refining away coarser factors (vitarka/vicāra in both vocabularies); the Yoga Sūtra's goal (puruṣa's isolation) and the Buddhist cessation are not claimed to be the same.

change: stages banded: 1 śodhana through ṣaṭkarma=B1; 2 dṛḍhatā through āsana=B2; 3 sthiratā through mudrā=B2; 4 dhairya through pratyāhāra=B3; 5 lāghava through prāṇāyāma=B2; 6 pratyakṣa through dhyāna=B5; 7 nirliptatva through samādhi=B7
reason: Each means is banded by the fruit the text assigns it (1.11) and the kind of practice of its chapter: cleansing = purification (B1); posture and seals = preparatory discipline (B2); withdrawal = B3; breath = B2 (kept in the text's non-monotonic order); 'direct perception in the self' through meditation = B5; untaintedness and 'liberation without doubt' through samādhi = B7.
Stage 7 is expanded into six kinds of samādhi in GhS 7.
Four limb-names shared (āsana, pratyāhāra, prāṇāyāma, dhyāna, samādhi); yama/niyama replaced by bodily cleansing; mudrā added; order of prāṇāyāma and pratyāhāra reversed.

change: stages banded: 1 prāṇāyāma=B2; 2 pratyāhāra=B3; 3 dhyāna=B3; 4 dhāraṇā=B3; 5 tarka=B4; 6 samādhi=B4; 7 seeing the golden-hued maker=B5; 8 making all one in the imperishable=B7
reason: The six limbs are banded by kind (breath B2; withdrawal, meditation, concentration B3; tarka and samādhi B4); the vision of the golden-hued maker and of the self 'by the self' is the first seeing (B5); making all one in the imperishable, faults no longer clinging, is liberation (B7).
Same count of six and three shared limb-names (pratyāhāra, dhyāna, prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, samādhi) in a different order, with anusmṛti for tarka; no historical claim is made here.
As above: six limbs with five shared names; Kālacakra has anusmṛti where the Maitrī has tarka.
Nātha six-limbed yoga (āsana instead of tarka).
Six-limbed yoga of the Yoga Upaniṣads.
The Amṛtanāda Upaniṣad's six limbs (pratyāhāra, dhyāna, prāṇāyāma, dhāraṇā, tarka, samādhi) keep tarka as in the Maitrī.

change: stages banded: 1 mantrayoga=B2; 2 layayoga=B3; 3 haṭhayoga=B2; 4 rājayoga=B7
reason: Banded by the kind of each yoga: mantra repetition and haṭha technique are preparatory discipline (B2); laya is dissolution of mind by one-pointed indications (B3); rājayoga is the goal-state the text describes as liberating (B7). The grading is by adhikāra (P4), not a single ladder.
The Yogatattva Upaniṣad repeats the same four yogas (it draws on the Dattātreyayogaśāstra).
Gorakṣa's Amaraughaprabodha names the same four yogas and grades them by practitioner.

change: stages banded: 1 ārambha=B2; 2 ghaṭa=B3; 3 paricaya=B4; 4 niṣpatti=B7
reason: Beginning = signs of breath-discipline (B2); ghaṭa = the conjunction of breaths and sense-withdrawal (B3); paricaya = breath and mind in the central channel with element-concentrations (B4); niṣpatti = rājayoga, samādhi of the one liberated while living (B7). Matches U29 (pth:siva-samhita-four-avasthas) and U04; U28 banded the HYP nāda version one band higher at the start (B3, B4, B4, B7), which reflects the HYP's own description.
The Haṭhayogapradīpikā's account of the same four stages through inner sound and the three knots.
The Śiva Saṃhitā's account of the same four stages.
The Yogatattva Upaniṣad's account of the same four stages.
Both describe the breath/kuṇḍalinī passing the knots or centres up the central channel.

change: stages banded: 1 śubhecchā=B0; 2 vicāraṇā=B2; 3 tanumānasā=B3; 4 sattvāpatti=B5; 5 asaṃsakti=B6; 6 padārthābhāvanī=B6; 7 turyagā=B7; 8 turyātīta=B7
reason: Good desire is the turning (B0); inquiry through scripture and practice is preparatory (B2); thinning of mind is withdrawal from objects (B3); the mind resting in the self (the 'knower of Brahman') is the first direct seeing (B5); non-attachment and non-perception of objects deepen it (B6); turyagā is liberation while living (B7) and turyātīta bodiless liberation (B7).
The Varāha Upaniṣad gives the same seven stages (tanumānasī, padārthabhāvanā as variant spellings).
The Mahā Upaniṣad pairs these seven stages of knowledge with seven stages of ignorance.
Vidyāraṇya's Pañcadaśī 7 gives a different sevenfold series of the jīva's states (ignorance → satisfaction).
Graded knowers in the Yoga tradition (the bhāṣya's four kinds of yogin).

change: stages banded: 1 citta-śuddhi through karma and upāsanā=B1; 2 sādhana-catuṣṭaya=B0; 3 guru-upasatti=B0; 4 śravaṇa=B2; 5 manana=B2; 6 nididhyāsana=B4; 7 aparokṣa-jñāna=B5; 8 jīvanmukti=B7; 9 the liberated one's life for the world=B8; 10 videhamukti=B7
reason: Purifying rites are B1; the fourfold means and approaching the teacher are qualification/entry (B0, kept in the tradition's order after B1); hearing and reflection are scriptural study (B2); contemplation as a flow of like cognitions is absorption with support (B4); the immediate knowledge 'I am Brahman' is the first seeing (B5); jīvanmukti (B7) and videhamukti (B7) are liberation; the knower's life for others is B8.
Expands stage 6 (the auxiliaries of nididhyāsana: savikalpa and nirvikalpa samādhi).
Śaṅkara-attributed fifteen limbs of 'rāja-yoga' re-described as knowledge; a parallel Advaita path.
Vidyāraṇya's Jīvanmuktiviveka uses the seven bhūmikās to grade Advaita knowers (stages 4-7 ~ this map's 7-9).
Dvaita also teaches śravaṇa-manana-nididhyāsana leading to aparokṣa-jñāna, but of the Lord as other than the self; Dvaita rejects the identity this map's stage 7 names.

change: stages banded: 1 iruvinaiyoppu, malaparipāka, śaktinipāta=B0; 2 caryā=B2; 3 kriyā=B2; 4 yoga=B4; 5 jñāna=B5; 6 sāyujya / aṇaintu nirral=B7; 7 worship of the devotees and the temple=B8
reason: The descent of grace is the entry (B0); caryā and kriyā are devotional/ritual practice (B2); yoga is inner absorption on Śiva (B4); jñāna begins with the guru-given seeing of Śiva in the soul (B5); union is liberation (B7); the freed soul's worship of devotees and temple is activity after liberation (B8).
The Tamil ten acts (tacakāriyam) articulate the jñāna-pāda's culmination.
Both lead through devotional practice to a relational culmination (union as servant; prema) rather than identity.
Both end in liberation through knowledge given by grace/teaching; the Siddhānta rejects Advaita's identity of soul and Śiva (sāyujya is inseparability, not identity).

change: stages banded: 1 āṇavopāya=B2; 2 śāktopāya=B4; 3 śāmbhavopāya=B5; 4 anupāya=B7
reason: Āṇava works with supports of breath, body, image, letter and place (B2, rising to B3-B4); śākta is contemplation purifying thought, still with a conceptual object (B4); śāmbhava is thought-free immersion through the teacher's awakening — recognition (B5); anupāya is the recognition that nothing remains to be done (B7). Because the means are assigned by grade of grace (P4), the bands mark kind, not a required sequence.
Both hold that recognition of one's own nature can be immediate for some while others proceed by graded means; not claimed to be the same recognition.
Dzogchen and the Trika both speak of a means-less recognition; each tradition's account of what is recognized differs and neither endorses the equation.

change: stages banded: 1 bhakta=B0; 2 māheśvara=B1; 3 prasādī=B3; 4 prāṇaliṅgī=B5; 5 śaraṇa=B6; 6 aikya=B7
reason: Banded through the six kinds of devotion the tradition itself pairs with the sthalas: faith (B0), steadiness in vows (B1), attentiveness/serenity of mind (B3), experience — recognition of the liṅga as consciousness (B5), bliss of union (B6), equal flavour — oneness (B7).
The 101 sub-sthalas of the Siddhāntaśikhāmaṇi subdivide these six.
Both ascend by kinds of devotion (faith → steadiness → … → union / prema).

change: stages banded: 1 śraddhā=B0; 2 sādhu-saṅga=B0; 3 bhajana-kriyā=B2; 4 anartha-nivṛtti=B1; 5 niṣṭhā=B3; 6 ruci=B4; 7 āsakti=B4; 8 bhāva=B5; 9 prema=B7
reason: Faith and holy company are entry (B0); practice is devotional discipline (B2); removal of unwanted things is purification (B1, kept in textual order); steadiness is one-pointed constancy (B3); taste and attachment are absorption in the object of devotion (B4); bhāva, the first 'ray' of love and the start of perfection (bhāva-bhakti), is the first direct manifestation (B5); prema, the final goal, is banded at the culmination (B7). Same as U16's pth:madhurya-kadambini-stages.
Viśvanātha Cakravartin's Mādhurya-kādambinī expounds the same nine stages (subdividing practice and the anarthas); bands identical.
Continues stage 9: prema → sneha → māna → praṇaya → rāga → anurāga → mahābhāva.
Nārada's aphorisms also lead from renunciation and company of the great to love.

change: stages banded: 1 mithyādṛṣṭi=unbanded; 2 sāsādana=unbanded; 3 samyag-mithyādṛṣṭi=B0; 4 avirata-samyagdṛṣṭi=B5; 5 deśavirata=B1; 6 pramatta-saṃyata=B1; 7 apramatta-saṃyata=B3; 8 apūrvakaraṇa=B4; 9 anivṛtti-bādara-sāmparāya=B6; 10 sūkṣma-sāmparāya=B6; 11 upaśānta-moha=B6; 12 kṣīṇa-moha=B6; 13 sayoga-kevalin=B7; 14 ayoga-kevalin=B7
reason: Stage 1 is the starting condition and 2 a stage of falling (unbanded); the mixed stage is the wavering threshold (B0); right view is the tradition's first real seeing (B5); vows are the ethical foundation (B1) — non-monotonic because the Jain path puts view before conduct (TS 1.1); careful restraint with virtuous meditation is B3; the first pure meditation with scriptural thought B4; the destruction/subsidence of passions B6; the omniscient states B7.
Umāsvāti's ten grades of karma-shedding (TS 9.45) run parallel to guṇasthānas 4-13.
Haribhadra's first four views fall within guṇasthāna 1; sthirā onward correspond to right view (4) and above; parā to kevala.
External self ~ guṇasthānas 1-3; internal self ~ 4-12; supreme self ~ 13-14 (Pūjyapāda's Samādhitantra).
The four pure meditations are distributed over guṇasthānas 8-14.

Right view (4) and stream-entry are both the first irreversible seeing that bounds the remaining rebirths; the Jain soul-doctrine and the Buddhist not-self teaching are not reconciled by this correspondence.

change: stages banded: 1 mitrā dṛṣṭi=B0; 2 tārā dṛṣṭi=B1; 3 balā dṛṣṭi=B2; 4 dīprā dṛṣṭi=B2; 5 sthirā dṛṣṭi=B5; 6 kāntā dṛṣṭi=B6; 7 prabhā dṛṣṭi=B6; 8 parā dṛṣṭi=B7
reason: Banded by the Jain criterion of view rather than by the paired Pātañjala limb where the two diverge: the sowing of the seeds of yoga (B0), observances (B1), steady posture and inner breath-control with hearing (B2), the breaking of the knot and right view in sthirā (B5), firm concentration and meditation with unattached activity (B6), absorption, omniscience and liberation in parā (B7).
Haribhadra pairs the views with Patañjali's limbs (YDS 16), reinterpreted inwardly; stated by the text itself.
The first four views lie within guṇasthāna 1 (ogha-dṛṣṭi); sthirā begins right view (4+); parā is kevala (13-14).
Haribhadra's four kinds of yogin grade the same practitioners by family and progress.

change: stages banded: 1 vikṣipta=unbanded; 2 yātāyāta=B3; 3 śliṣṭa=B4; 4 sulīna=B4; 5 unmanībhāva=B5
reason: The scattered mind is the starting condition (unbanded); the mind that goes and returns is beginning one-pointedness (B3); the clinging and dissolved minds are stable blissful absorption (B4); the no-mind state in which the self is realised is the first seeing (B5).
Graded minds/practitioners in the Yoga tradition; Vyāsa's five levels of mind (kṣipta … niruddha, YBh 1.1) are a closer analogue.

change: stages banded: 1 adhisīla-sikkhā=B1; 2 adhicitta-sikkhā=B4; 3 adhipaññā-sikkhā=B5; 4 vimutti=B7
reason: Virtue is the ethical foundation (B1); higher mind is the four jhānas (B4); higher wisdom is seeing the four truths as they are (B5, matured through B6); the mind freed from the effluents is liberation (B7).
The Visuddhimagga expounds its seven purifications within the frame of virtue, concentration and understanding.
The gradual training of DN 2 / MN 27 unfolds the three trainings step by step.
Ethical restraints → concentration → discernment in both; the Yoga Sūtra's goal (isolation of puruṣa) is not the Buddhist liberation.

change: stages banded: 1 upacāra-samādhi=B3; 2 paṭhama jhāna=B4; 3 dutiya jhāna=B4; 4 tatiya jhāna=B4; 5 catuttha jhāna=B4; 6 ākāsānañcāyatana=B4; 7 viññāṇañcāyatana=B4; 8 ākiñcaññāyatana=B4; 9 nevasaññānāsaññāyatana=B4; 10 saññāvedayitanirodha=B6
reason: Access concentration is one-pointedness before absorption (B3); the four jhānas and four formless attainments are absorption with support — the formless ones still have an object (space, consciousness, nothingness) and by themselves do not lead to awakening (MN 26) (B4); cessation is restricted to noble persons after seeing and is banded B6.
Graded absorptions dropping coarser factors; not claimed identical.
The Laṅkāvatāra's four dhyānas grade meditation by its object rather than by factors.

change: stages banded: 1 sīla-visuddhi=B1; 2 citta-visuddhi=B4; 3 diṭṭhi-visuddhi=B4; 4 kaṅkhāvitaraṇa-visuddhi=B4; 5 maggāmagga-ñāṇadassana-visuddhi=B4; 6 paṭipadā-ñāṇadassana-visuddhi=B4; 7 ñāṇadassana-visuddhi=B5; 8 anupādā parinibbāna=B7
reason: Virtue is B1; purification of mind is access and absorption (B4); purifications 3-6 are mundane insight whose object is still conditioned formations — banded B4 by this unit's rule; the seventh, knowledge of the supramundane paths, starts at the first seeing of nibbāna (B5); the goal, final nibbāna without clinging, is B7.
The insight knowledges are distributed over purifications 3-7.
Pa-Auk's teaching follows the Visuddhimagga order (U37 bands its mundane insight B5-B6; see cpt:path-map-correspondence).
Purification 1 = virtue, 2 = concentration, 3-7 = understanding.

change: stages banded: 1 nāmarūpa-pariccheda-ñāṇa=B4; 2 paccaya-pariggaha-ñāṇa=B4; 3 sammasana-ñāṇa=B4; 4 udayabbaya-ñāṇa=B4; 5 bhaṅga-ñāṇa=B4; 6 bhaya-ñāṇa=B4; 7 ādīnava-ñāṇa=B4; 8 nibbidā-ñāṇa=B4; 9 muñcitukamyatā-ñāṇa=B4; 10 paṭisaṅkhā-ñāṇa=B4; 11 saṅkhārupekkhā-ñāṇa=B4; 12 anuloma-ñāṇa=B4; 13 gotrabhū-ñāṇa=B5; 14 magga-ñāṇa=B5; 15 phala-ñāṇa=B5; 16 paccavekkhaṇa-ñāṇa=B5
reason: Knowledges 1-12 are mundane insight whose object is conditioned formations (B4 by this unit's rule); change-of-lineage, path, fruition and reviewing mark the first seeing of nibbāna (B5); the series recurs for the higher paths (B6-B7).
Knowledges 1-2 fall in purifications 3-4, 3-4 in 5, 4-12 in 6, 13-16 around and in 7.
Mahāsi Sayadaw's practical account of the same knowledges through noting.
Sarvāstivāda: heat, peak, patience and supreme mundane quality precede the path of seeing, as mundane insight precedes the path here.

change: stages banded: 1 sotāpattiyaṅga=B0; 2 sotāpatti-magga=B5; 3 sotāpanna=B5; 4 sakadāgāmi-magga=B6; 5 sakadāgāmī=B6; 6 anāgāmi-magga=B6; 7 anāgāmī=B6; 8 arahatta-magga=B6; 9 arahant=B7
reason: The factors for stream-entry are the entry (B0); the stream-entry path and fruit are the first seeing (B5); the higher paths and fruits up to the path of arahantship deepen it (B6); arahantship is final liberation (B7).
Sarvāstivāda has the same four fruits and eight persons, with a different account of the path of seeing (fifteen/sixteen moments).
Stream-entry corresponds to the path of seeing, the higher paths to the path of cultivation, arahantship to no-more-learning, in the Abhidharma and Mahāyāna presentations.
Stream-entry and Jain right view are both the first irreversible seeing that bounds the remaining births; the not-self teaching and the Jain soul-doctrine are not reconciled by this.

change: stages banded: 1 sati-sambojjhaṅga=B3; 2 dhammavicaya-sambojjhaṅga=B4; 3 vīriya-sambojjhaṅga=B4; 4 pīti-sambojjhaṅga=B4; 5 passaddhi-sambojjhaṅga=B4; 6 samādhi-sambojjhaṅga=B4; 7 upekkhā-sambojjhaṅga=B4; 8 vijjā-vimutti=B7
reason: Mindfulness is one-pointed attention (B3); investigation through equanimity are the matured factors of meditation still working with their objects (B4); true knowledge and liberation are the fruit (B7). No separate B5-B6 stage is named by the sutta.
MN 118's sixteen steps fulfil the establishments of mindfulness, which fulfil these factors.
Another canonical sequence leading through rapture, tranquillity and concentration to knowledge and liberation.

change: stages banded: 1 sīla-visuddhi=B1; 2 citta-visuddhi by khaṇika-samādhi=B3; 3 knowledges 1-3=B4; 4 knowledge 4=B4; 5 knowledges 5-10=B4; 6 knowledge 11=B4; 7 knowledges 12-13=B5; 8 knowledges 14-15=B5; 9 knowledge 16 and after=B6

change: stages banded: 1 saṃbhāra-mārga=B2; 2 prayoga-mārga=B4; 3 darśana-mārga=B5; 4 bhāvanā-mārga=B6; 5 aśaikṣa-mārga / niṣṭhā-mārga=B7; 6 buddha-karma=B8
reason: Accumulation = training and gathering (B2); preparation = conceptual insight into emptiness/mind-only joined to calm (B4); seeing = the first direct non-conceptual seeing (B5); cultivation through the grounds (B6); no-more-learning = buddhahood/arhatship (B7); the buddhas' spontaneous activity (B8).
Xuanzang's five stages of the path to cognition-only (資糧, 加行, 通達, 修習, 究竟) are the five paths.
The Sarvāstivāda path has the same preparatory aids (heat, peak, patience, supreme mundane) and the paths of seeing, cultivation and no-more-learning.
Path of seeing = first ground; path of cultivation = grounds 2-10; no-more-learning = buddhahood.
In the Abhidharma and Mahāyāna presentations stream-entry is on the path of seeing and arhatship at no-more-learning.
Padampa Sangye arranges Pacification along these five paths.
Kagyu masters correlate the four yogas with the five paths in differing ways (Moonbeams).

change: stages banded: 1 pramuditā=B5; 2 vimalā=B6; 3 prabhākarī=B6; 4 arciṣmatī=B6; 5 sudurjayā=B6; 6 abhimukhī=B6; 7 dūraṅgamā=B6; 8 acalā=B6; 9 sādhumatī=B6; 10 dharmameghā=B6; 11 buddha-bhūmi=B7
reason: The first ground is the path of seeing (B5); grounds 2-10 are the path of cultivation (B6) — including the tenth, whose activity-character is noted but which precedes buddhahood; the buddha-ground is B7.
Candrakīrti's Madhyamakāvatāra follows the same ten grounds and perfections; bands identical.
The Lokottaravāda Mahāvastu has a different list of ten grounds (durārohā …).
The Bodhisattvabhūmi's thirteen abodes include the ten grounds within a longer series.
The East Asian fifty-two stages place the ten grounds after the ten faiths, abodes, practices and dedications.
Ground 1 = path of seeing; 2-10 = path of cultivation.

change: stages banded: 1 cittasthāpana / sems 'jog pa=B3; 2 saṃsthāpana / rgyun du 'jog pa=B3; 3 avasthāpana / glan te 'jog pa=B3; 4 upasthāpana / nye bar 'jog pa=B3; 5 damana / dul bar byed pa=B3; 6 śamana / zhi bar byed pa=B3; 7 vyupaśamana / rnam par zhi bar byed pa=B3; 8 ekotīkaraṇa / rtse gcig tu byed pa=B3; 9 samādhāna / mnyam par 'jog pa=B3; 10 śamatha proper=B4
reason: All nine settlings are the progressive stabilizing of one-pointed attention (B3); calm abiding proper, marked by pliancy, is stable absorption with support (B4).

Mahāmudrā śamatha uses the nine settlings (Moonbeams).
Calm abiding proper corresponds to access to the first dhyāna in both Abhidharma systems.

change: stages banded: 1 reliance on the spiritual teacher=B0; 2 leisure and endowment=B0; 3 small scope: death and the lower realms=B0; 4 small scope: refuge and karma=B1; 5 middle scope: the faults of saṃsāra and =B0; 6 middle scope: the three trainings=B1; 7 great scope: the mind of awakening=B0; 8 great scope: the deeds=B2; 9 calm abiding=B4; 10 insight=B4; 11 entering the Vajrayāna=unbanded
reason: Banded by the kind of each topic: reliance, the precious life and the turnings of each scope (death, saṃsāra's faults, the mind of awakening) are entry/turning (B0); karma, refuge-ethics and the three trainings are the ethical foundation (B1); the perfections are practice (B2); calm abiding proper and conceptual insight are B4; the Vajrayāna hand-over is unbanded.
Tsongkhapa's condensation: renunciation (middle scope), the mind of awakening (great scope), the correct view (insight).
Gampopa's Jewel Ornament (Kagyu) follows the same Kadam stages.
The Sakya 'parting from the four attachments' condenses the same scopes.
The Nyingma outer preliminaries cover the same ground as the small and middle scopes.

change: stages banded: 1 rtse gcig=B4; 2 rtse gcig=B4; 3 rtse gcig=B4; 4 spros bral=B5; 5 spros bral=B6; 6 spros bral=B6; 7 ro gcig=B6; 8 ro gcig=B6; 9 ro gcig=B6; 10 sgom med=B6; 11 sgom med=B6; 12 sgom med=B7
reason: One-pointedness is stable absorption with experiences (B4); lesser simplicity is where many masters place the path of seeing (B5), its higher levels deepening (B6); one taste and non-meditation up to its middling level are cultivation (B6); greater non-meditation is buddhahood (B7). These correlations are contested within the Kagyu (P4 applies; see notes).
Expands stage 7 of U46's Moonbeams map.
Tilopa's torrent–river–ocean describes the same deepening in three images.
Kagyu masters correlate the four yogas with the five paths and ten grounds differently; Moonbeams records the views.
Drikung's fivefold Mahāmudrā arranges the same practice by five points rather than stages.

change: stages banded: 1 chos nyid mngon sum=B5; 2 nyams gong 'phel=B6; 3 rig pa tshad phebs=B6; 4 chos nyid zad pa=B7
reason: The first vision, direct perception of dharmatā on the basis of recognized awareness, is banded B5; increase and full measure are deepening (B6); exhaustion of phenomena in dharmatā is the final fruit (B7). Banded cautiously because the tradition denies that these are stages of production (see tradition_objection).
The four visions are the direct-crossing stage of Jigme Lingpa's Yeshe Lama map (U45).
Both describe the ripening of the recognition of mind's nature to its exhaustion/non-meditation; neither tradition treats them as identical systems.
Both are completion-level practices in which appearances of light arise and are recognized as the mind's own display; methods and views differ.

change: stages banded: 1 pratyāhāra=B3; 2 dhyāna=B4; 3 prāṇāyāma=B4; 4 dhāraṇā=B4; 5 anusmṛti=B4; 6 samādhi=B6; 7 fruit: the Ādibuddha's gnosis=B7
reason: Withdrawal with its signs is B3; meditative stability on empty form, vitality-control, retention and recollection are absorption with support (B4); the samādhi branch spans the first seeing through cultivation (banded B6 with a note) and its completion, the Ādibuddha's gnosis, is B7.
Same six branch-names in the same order (Guhyasamāja 18.138); Kālacakra gives them its own content.
Six limbs with five shared names (tarka in the Maitrī where the Kālacakra has anusmṛti).
The six branches are the Kālacakra's completion stage.

change: stages banded: 1 tshogs lam=B2; 2 sbyor lam=B4; 3 mthong lam=B5; 4 sgom lam=B6; 5 mi slob lam=B7
reason: Banded as the general five paths (B2, B4, B5, B6, B7), on which the Pacification instructions are arranged.
The general five-path frame applied to Pacification.

change: stages banded: 1 xun niu 尋牛=B0; 2 jian ji 見跡=B2; 3 jian niu 見牛=B5; 4 de niu 得牛=B6; 5 mu niu 牧牛=B6; 6 qi niu gui jia 騎牛歸家=B6; 7 wang niu cun ren 忘牛存人=B6; 8 ren niu ju wang 人牛俱忘=B7; 9 fan ben huan yuan 返本還源=B7; 10 ru chan chui shou 入鄽垂手=B8
reason: Searching is the turning (B0); seeing the traces through the teachings is study (B2); seeing the ox is the first glimpse of one's nature (B5); catching, herding, riding home and forgetting the ox are cultivation after seeing (B6); the empty circle and the return to the source are liberation (B7); entering the marketplace is activity after liberation (B8).
Puming's series ends in the empty circle (Kuoan's 8); Kuoan adds returning to the source and entering the marketplace.
Another Chan map ending in return to the world of distinctions.
Seeing the ox then taming it matches 'sudden awakening, gradual cultivation'.

change: stages banded: 1 seeking buddha in one's own mind=B0; 2 tono 頓悟=B5; 3 chŏmsu 漸修=B6; 4 chŭng 證=B7
reason: The turning to seek buddha in the mind is B0; sudden (understanding-)awakening is the first seeing (B5); gradual cultivation after awakening is B6 by definition; realization through cultivation is B7.
Jinul adopts Zongmi's 'sudden awakening followed by gradual cultivation' and cites his frozen-pond simile.
Seeing the ox then taming it.
Immediate recognition for some, graded means for others.

change: stages banded: 1 hosshin 発心=B0; 2 shugyō 修行 — shikan taza=B6; 3 bodai 菩提=B5; 4 nehan 涅槃=B7
reason: Banded with care: arousing the mind B0; practice-in-realization B6 (Dōgen: 'practice on top of realization'); awakening B5; nirvāṇa B7 — non-monotonic because Dōgen denies sequence (recorded as the tradition's objection, not as a band).
Both are Zen maps, but Dōgen rejects treating practice as a means to a later awakening, which the pictures' sequence suggests.
Jinul puts cultivation after awakening; Dōgen makes them one — 'practice on top of realization' is close to Jinul's order, but Dōgen denies any sequence.
Both traditions deny that practice produces what is already complete ('the Way is fundamentally complete'; the all-creating king has nothing to do).

change: stages banded: 1 liji 理即=unbanded; 2 mingziji 名字即=B0; 3 guanxingji 觀行即=B3; 4 xiangsiji 相似即=B4; 5 fenzhenji 分真即=B5; 6 jiujingji 究竟即=B7
reason: Identity in principle is the starting condition (unbanded); verbal identity is hearing and faith (B0); contemplative practice is B3; resemblance — wisdom resembling the middle way, ignorance only subdued — is B4; partial truth begins with the first breaking of ignorance and seeing of buddha-nature (B5; its later stages B6); ultimate identity is wondrous awakening (B7).

Zhiyi maps the perfect teaching's stages onto the six identities: resemblance = ten faiths; partial truth = the forty-one stages from the first abode to equal awakening; ultimate = wondrous awakening.
Resemblance ~ preparation; partial truth begins with the first seeing of buddha-nature.

change: stages banded: 1 shixin 十信=B0; 2 shizhu 十住=B2; 3 shixing 十行=B2; 4 shi huixiang 十迴向=B4; 5 shidi 十地=B5; 6 dengjue 等覺=B6; 7 miaojue 妙覺=B7
reason: The ten faiths are entry (B0); the abodes and practices are the worthies' training (B2); the dedications are the threshold group (B4); the grounds begin the sagely stages with the first seeing (B5); equal awakening is the last cultivation (B6); wondrous awakening is buddhahood (B7).

change: stages banded: 1 dunwu 頓悟=B5; 2 fa beizhi yuan 發悲智願=B6; 3 suifen xiuxi 隨分修習=B6; 4 da putixin xianfa 大菩提心顯發=B6; 5 zhi faxing 知法性=B6; 6 suishun xiu liudu, wofa shuangwang 隨順修六度=B6; 7 yu se zizai 於色自在=B6; 8 yu xin zizai 於心自在=B6; 9 jiujing jue 究竟覺=B7; 10 da jue zun 大覺尊=B7

change: stages banded: 1 ishō teiyō shin 異生羝羊心=unbanded; 2 gudō jisai shin 愚童持齋心=B1; 3 yōdō mui shin 嬰童無畏心=B2; 4 yuiun muga shin 唯蘊無我心=unbanded; 5 batsugō inshu shin 拔業因種心=unbanded; 6 taen daijō shin 他縁大乘心=unbanded; 7 kakushin fushō shin 覺心不生心=unbanded; 8 ichidō mui shin 一道無爲心=unbanded; 9 gokumu jishō shin 極無自性心=unbanded; 10 himitsu shōgon shin 秘密莊嚴心=B7
